questions.q: What consistent story did the ARMA, GARCH, and factor-model results tell when read together?
options: That the universe has no usable structure of any kind

That this universe's real dynamics live in volatility (GARCH found strong persistence), not in mean-level return predictability (ARMA correctly found little), while the factor model recovered betas close to their true simulation values
That GARCH found nothing while ARMA found everything
That the factor model and the sample covariance were identical in every entry
questions.explain: ARMA correctly found little mean-level structure (consistent with a universe simulated with no autocorrelation in the mean), GARCH found real, substantial volatility persistence, and the factor model's estimated betas tracked the true simulation values closely -- three tools giving one coherent reading of the same underlying design.

questions.q: Why does the lesson treat COBM's fitted GARCH persistence (0.764) landing well below its 0.96 simulation target as an honest limitation rather than a failure?
options: Because GARCH models never produce accurate results
Because it demonstrates real sampling uncertainty in GARCH estimation on a ~1,000-day (four-year) sample, which is a short history even when the true data-generating process is known exactly
Because COBM's true persistence was actually 0.764
Because the arch package has a known bug for Materials-sector tickers
questions.explain: The simulated universe's short history (about four years of trading days) is explicitly named as a limitation -- GARCH parameters carry real estimation uncertainty on a sample this size, which is exactly what COBM's gap between fitted (0.764) and true (0.96) persistence shows.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does a one-factor covariance model trade off against the plain sample covariance?
options: It has no tradeoff -- it is strictly more accurate in every case
It trades some bias (the imposed single-factor structure may not be fully correct) for less estimation variance (fewer parameters to estimate, which can be more stable on short samples)
It trades accuracy for slower computation time
It eliminates the need to estimate any betas at all
questions.explain: The factor model imposes structure (all co-movement running through one common factor), which is a real simplification, in exchange for estimating far fewer parameters than a full sample covariance matrix -- a standard bias-variance tradeoff, not a guaranteed improvement in accuracy.

questions.q: What should a strong portfolio presentation of this capstone include, according to this lesson?
options: Only the final numerical results table, with no code or discussion of limitations
The simulation and modeling code, a results table, and a written limitations summary naming the small universe, short sample, and model-selection noise explicitly
A guarantee that the model will be profitable in live trading
A comparison against a machine-learning model trained on real market data
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly lists the reproducible code, a results table, and a written limitations summary (small universe, short sample, model-selection noise) as what a strong presentation of this project includes -- being clear about what the results do and don't show.

The same course repeated from Chapter 1
A course outside the Quantitative Developer / Researcher path entirely
